description: Sun-bleached plates cracked round a heart of gold, all a Dewling leaves. Blows land like a dropped weight, and dazzle.
lore: Cutlers keep the seams turned outward, for the flash: whatever takes the hit stands blinking at nothing for a second, and there is no light anywhere about to account for what it thinks it just saw. Bedded the wrong way, it is merely heavy.

The sorters grade them by how little colour is left. A sand-brown one came off ground somebody still walks. The bone-pale ones, seams gone nearly white, come off meadows a great many people remember and none of them visit any more, and fetch double. A strange way to price anything; the trade stopped finding it strange long ago.

[[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] came to the sorting sheds last autumn and copied ten years of grade-books into [[lore/the_chronicle|the Chronicle]], price by price, and would not say what she wanted them for. She did not need to. Anyone can read a column that only climbs: every season the [[monsters/forest_poring|Dewlings]] come up a little paler, off a few more meadows going unwalked.
gm_notes: The climbing grade-books are the Thinning read through a price list — abandonment measured in bleach. Never give Bettany's numbers or name which meadows emptied; the column climbing is all that ships.
